title: Define LinkStore and UserStore traits with core data models
body:
## Description

Define the async trait interfaces for LinkStore and UserStore that abstract over SQLite (standalone) and PostgreSQL (platform). Also define the shared data models: Link, NewLink, UpdateLink, ClickMeta, LinkStats, User, NewUser, UpdateUser.

These traits are the foundation for all database operations. Every handler depends on them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `LinkStore` trait defined with all methods: get_by_code, create, update, delete, list_by_user, record_click, get_stats, export_all, import_batch
- [ ] `UserStore` trait defined with all methods: get_by_id, get_by_email, get_by_nostr_pubkey, get_by_api_key, create, update, link_nostr
- [ ] All shared model structs defined in models.rs
- [ ] Feature flags configured in Cargo.toml: standalone (rusqlite, askama, argon2) and platform (sqlx, brickos-auth)

## Technical Notes

- Use `#[async_trait]` from the async-trait crate
- Traits must be `Send + Sync` for use with axum
- Models should derive Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug
- Link model includes: id, code, target_url, title, tags, user_id, is_active, expires_at, created_at, updated_at, click_count

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 6.3 (Database Traits)

## Description

Build the configuration system that reads from `config.toml` with environment variable overrides. This determines standalone vs. platform mode, database path, server bind address, JWT secret, NOSTR relay list, and all runtime settings.

- [ ] Sensible defaults for standalone mode
- [ ] Example config.toml created (config.example.toml)
- [ ] Config validation on startup (fail fast on missing required values like jwt_secret)

- Use `serde` + `toml` crate for TOML parsing
- Use `config` crate or manual ENV layering
- JWT secret must be at least 32 bytes
- Default bind: 127.0.0.1:3000
- Default mode: standalone

title: Create SQLite database migrations
body:
## Description

Write the initial SQLite migration (001_initial.sql) that creates all tables needed for standalone mode: users, links, clicks, api_keys. Include indexes for the redirect hot path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] users table: id, email, password_hash, display_name, nostr_pubkey, api_key_hash, role (admin/user), is_active, created_at, updated_at, last_login_at
- [ ] links table: id, code, target_url, title, tags (JSON), user_id (FK), is_active, expires_at, created_at, updated_at
- [ ] clicks table: id, link_id (FK), visitor_hash (SHA256), referrer_domain, country_code, clicked_at
- [ ] Unique index on links.code for redirect hot path
- [ ] Index on links.user_id for dashboard queries
- [ ] Index on clicks.link_id + clicks.clicked_at for stats queries
- [ ] Migration runs on startup if DB is empty
- [ ] visitor_hash uses SHA256(IP + code + date) - no raw IP storage

## Technical Notes

- Use rusqlite for migration execution
- Store migrations in migrations/sqlite/001_initial.sql
- WAL mode enabled for concurrent reads during redirects
- STRICT mode for type safety

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 4.1 (Click privacy), Section 6.1 (migrations/sqlite/)

Build the email/password authentication flow: registration, login, JWT token issuance, token refresh, and Argon2id password hashing. First registered user auto-becomes admin. Admin can disable further registration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] POST /auth/register creates user with Argon2id hashed password
- [ ] POST /auth/login verifies password, returns JWT
- [ ] POST /auth/refresh issues new JWT from valid existing token
- [ ] JWT contains: sub (user_id), role, exp (24h default, configurable)
- [ ] First registered user gets admin role automatically
- [ ] Registration can be disabled via config or admin setting
- [ ] AuthProvider trait defined with EmailPasswordProvider implementation
- [ ] Rate limiting on /auth/login: 10 attempts per minute per IP
- [ ] Password validation: minimum 8 characters
- [ ] Unit tests for registration, login, token refresh flows

## Technical Notes

- Use argon2 crate with default (recommended) params
- Use jsonwebtoken crate for JWT
- JWT secret from config
- AuthRequest enum: EmailPassword { email, password }
- AuthResult: { token, user, created }

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 4.2.1 (Email + Password), Section 4.2.4 (AuthProvider Architecture)

title: Implement NOSTR NIP-98 authentication
body:
## Description

Build passwordless authentication using NOSTR keypair signatures (NIP-98). Verify kind 27235 events, check timestamp freshness, validate secp256k1 signatures, and auto-create accounts for new pubkeys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] POST /auth/nostr accepts NIP-98 signed event
- [ ] Validates event kind is 27235
- [ ] Validates 'u' tag matches endpoint URL
- [ ] Validates created_at within 60 seconds of server time
- [ ] Validates secp256k1 signature against pubkey
- [ ] Existing user by pubkey: issues JWT
- [ ] New pubkey: auto-creates user account, issues JWT, returns created: true
- [ ] NostrNip98Provider implements AuthProvider trait
- [ ] NIP-98 event verification module in nostr/nip98.rs
- [ ] Unit tests for valid event, expired event, wrong kind, invalid signature

## Technical Notes

- Use nostr crate or secp256k1 crate for signature verification
- Event ID is SHA256 of serialized event (NIP-01)
- Browser integration via NIP-07: window.nostr.signEvent()
- Fallback: paste nsec (client-side signing only, nsec never sent to server)

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 4.2.2 (NOSTR NIP-98)

title: Implement redirect handler (hot path)
body:
## Description

Build the GET /{code} redirect handler. This is the performance-critical hot path - must resolve in under 10ms p95. Lookup code in LinkStore, return 301 redirect. Handle deactivated links (410 Gone), expired links, and missing codes (404).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GET /{code} returns 301 redirect to target_url for active links
- [ ] GET /{code} returns 410 Gone for deactivated links
- [ ] GET /{code} returns 404 for unknown codes
- [ ] Expired links (expires_at < now) return 410 Gone
- [ ] Click is recorded asynchronously (do not block redirect response)
- [ ] No authentication required
- [ ] Target URL validation rejects javascript: and data: schemes
- [ ] Latency target: < 10ms p95
- [ ] GET /{code}+ returns public click count as JSON

## Technical Notes

- Use axum router with path parameter
- Click recording should be spawned as a background task (tokio::spawn) to not block the redirect
- The code lookup must use the indexed path in SQLite
- Rate limit: 1000/min per IP

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 4.1 (Redirect), Section 5 (NFR: redirect latency < 10ms)

title: Implement click tracking with privacy-preserving hashing
body:
## Description

Build the click tracking system that records clicks without storing raw IP addresses. Use SHA256(IP + code + daily_salt) for visitor deduplication. Extract referrer domain and country code from request headers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Click recorded with: link_id, visitor_hash, referrer_domain, country_code, clicked_at
- [ ] visitor_hash = SHA256(IP + code + date) - rotates daily
- [ ] No raw IP address stored anywhere
- [ ] No user agent stored
- [ ] Referrer domain extracted from Referer header (domain only, not full URL)
- [ ] Country code from CF-IPCountry or X-Country-Code header (optional)
- [ ] Stats endpoint returns: total clicks, daily breakdown, top referrer domains
- [ ] Click recording is async (does not block redirect)

## Technical Notes

- Use sha2 crate for SHA256
- Daily salt = date string (YYYY-MM-DD), not a secret
- ClickMeta struct: { visitor_hash, referrer_domain, country_code }
- Background task via tokio::spawn for recording

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 4.1 (Click privacy: SHA256(IP + code + date))

## Description

Build the full REST API for programmatic link management. All endpoints authenticate via JWT (from email or NOSTR login) or API key. Covers create, read, update, delete, list, stats, import, export, and user settings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GET /api/v1/links - list user's links with pagination
- [ ] POST /api/v1/links - create link (auto-generate or custom code)
- [ ] GET /api/v1/links/{id} - get link detail
- [ ] PUT /api/v1/links/{id} - update link (target_url, title, tags, is_active)
- [ ] DELETE /api/v1/links/{id} - permanent delete
- [ ] GET /api/v1/links/{id}/stats - click analytics for a link
- [ ] GET /api/v1/links/export - export all links as JSON
- [ ] POST /api/v1/links/import - import links from JSON array
- [ ] GET /api/v1/me - current user info
- [ ] PUT /api/v1/me/settings - update user settings
- [ ] POST /api/v1/me/api-key - generate/regenerate API key
- [ ] GET /health - service health + version (no auth)
- [ ] All auth-required endpoints accept JWT Bearer token or API key
- [ ] Custom code validation: 3-30 chars, lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens
- [ ] Rate limit on POST /api/v1/links: 50/day per user

## Technical Notes

- Use axum with extractors for auth middleware
- API key auth: lookup by SHA256 hash of provided key
- Auto-generated codes: 6 chars, base62 (a-z, 0-9)
- Return 409 Conflict if custom code already exists

title: Implement NIP-89 app listing publisher
body:
## Description

On startup (if configured with NOSTR private key and relay list), publish a kind 31990 app listing event to NOSTR relays. This makes the Sovereign Link instance discoverable by NOSTR clients that support NIP-89 app recommendations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On startup, if nostr_private_key and nostr_relays are configured, publish NIP-89 event
- [ ] Event kind: 31990 (replaceable parameterized)
- [ ] Tags: d=sovereign-link, k=1, web=base_url, web=github_source
- [ ] Content: JSON with name, about, website, nips: [98, 89]
- [ ] Event signed with configured private key
- [ ] Published to all configured relays
- [ ] Republish on startup (replaceable event updates existing)
- [ ] If no NOSTR key configured, skip silently (no error)
- [ ] Module: nostr/nip89.rs

## Technical Notes

- Use nostr crate for event creation and signing
- Use nostr-sdk or raw WebSocket for relay publishing
- Replaceable event: relays keep only the latest version per d-tag
- Fire-and-forget: do not block startup on relay responses

## References

- Spec: 002 Section 4.5 (NOSTR Distribution NIP-89)

title: Create brickos PostgreSQL schema and move platform tables
body:
## Description

Phase 1 of schema elevation: create the `brickos` schema in PostgreSQL and move all 39 platform tables from `public` schema using ALTER TABLE SET SCHEMA. Update search_path so SHI continues working without code changes. This is the foundation for multi-app platform support.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS brickos
- [ ] Move all Category 1-6 tables (39 tables) via ALTER TABLE SET SCHEMA brickos
- [ ] Identity & Auth: users, refresh_tokens, email_verifications, user_mfa
- [ ] Organizations: organizations, org_members, app_roles, data_shares, audit_log
- [ ] Licensing & Billing: subscriptions, payment_events, btc_payments, refunds, invoices, invoice_line_items, payment_methods_cache, customer_tax_ids, payment_gateway_status, promotions, promotion_redemptions, user_licenses, license_events, affiliate_clicks, affiliate_conversions, affiliate_payouts, affiliate_commission_rates
- [ ] Communication: email_campaigns, email_sends, push_subscriptions, newsletter_subscribers, contact_submissions
- [ ] Audit: data_access_log, db_audit_log, pgaudit_events, content_audit_log
- [ ] Infrastructure: app_prefixes, short_links, short_link_clicks, search_index
- [ ] ALTER DATABASE SET search_path = public, brickos
- [ ] All existing SHI queries continue working without code changes
- [ ] Foreign keys and indexes follow tables automatically
- [ ] Migration is reversible (script to move tables back to public)

## Technical Notes

- ALTER TABLE SET SCHEMA is metadata-only, instantaneous, no data copy
- Cross-schema foreign keys work natively in PostgreSQL
- Run during low-traffic window but no downtime required
- Test on staging first with a copy of production data
- search_path order matters: public first (SHI tables), then brickos

## References

- Spec: 004 Section 7 Phase 1 (Schema Move)
- Spec: 004 Section 3 (Complete Table Classification)

title: Create service_accounts and reserved_codes tables in brickos schema
body:
## Description

Create the new platform tables that do not exist yet: service_accounts (for cross-app API access), service_account_keys (for key rotation), and reserved_codes (for preventing URL code collisions). These are created directly in the brickos schema.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] brickos.service_accounts table: id, name (unique), display_name, org_id (FK organizations), api_key_hash, scopes (TEXT[]), rate_limit_daily, is_active, last_used_at, created_by (FK users), created_at, rotated_at
- [ ] brickos.service_account_keys table: id, service_account_id (FK), api_key_hash, expires_at, created_at
- [ ] brickos.reserved_codes table: code (PK), reason, reserved_by (FK users), reserved_at
- [ ] Insert BrickOS platform org if not exists (well-known UUID 00000000-...)
- [ ] Seed reserved codes: shi, health, voice, signal, link, links, exchange, finance, vote, govern, almanac, energy, identity, id, relay, api, admin, app, docs, help, status, new, login, register, bitcoin, btc, nostr, brickos, brick, book, podcast, prague, btcprague
- [ ] Index on service_accounts.api_key_hash for auth lookups
- [ ] Index on service_accounts.org_id for org-scoped queries

## Technical Notes

- service_accounts support key rotation: two active keys during overlap period
- API keys stored as SHA256 hash, never plaintext
- Scopes are PostgreSQL TEXT[] array: ['links:create', 'links:read', 'links:stats']
- Reserved codes prevent both URL codes and org slugs from being claimed

## References

- Spec: 004 Section 9 (New Platform Tables)
- Spec: 003 Section 5 (Reserved Short URL Codes)
- Spec: 003 Section 6 (Service Account Security)

title: Create migration ownership structure in packages/brickos-db
body:
## Description

Establish the migration ownership split so platform migrations live in packages/brickos-db/ and app-specific migrations stay in their respective app directories. This prevents future migration conflicts between apps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create packages/brickos-db/ directory structure
- [ ] packages/brickos-db/migrations/ with numbered migration files:
  - 001_create_brickos_schema.sql
  - 002_identity_tables.sql
  - 003_organization_tables.sql
  - 004_billing_tables.sql
  - 005_communication_tables.sql
  - 006_audit_tables.sql
  - 007_infrastructure_tables.sql
  - 008_service_accounts.sql
  - 009_reserved_codes.sql
- [ ] Each migration is idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS)
- [ ] Migration runner or documentation for execution order
- [ ] SHI migrations renumbered or documented to depend on brickos-db
- [ ] README in packages/brickos-db/ explaining ownership model

## Technical Notes

- These migrations define the CREATE TABLE statements for all brickos schema tables
- They are the source of truth - the ALTER TABLE SET SCHEMA approach is for the initial transition
- New BrickOS apps depend on packages/brickos-db being migrated first
- Consider sqlx migrate or a simple migration runner

## References

- Spec: 004 Section 7 Phase 4 (Migration Ownership Split)

title: Implement service account API and authentication
body:
## Description

Build the API endpoints for managing service accounts and the authentication middleware that validates service account API keys. Service accounts enable cross-app API access (e.g., Sovereign Voice creating links via Sovereign Link).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] POST /api/v1/admin/service-accounts - create service account (platform_admin only)
- [ ] GET /api/v1/admin/service-accounts - list service accounts
- [ ] POST /api/v1/admin/service-accounts/{id}/rotate - generate new key (old key active for 24h)
- [ ] DELETE /api/v1/admin/service-accounts/{id}/keys/{key_id} - revoke specific key
- [ ] Auth middleware: check Authorization header against service_account_keys.api_key_hash
- [ ] Scope enforcement: service account can only access permitted endpoints
- [ ] Rate limiting: enforce rate_limit_daily per service account
- [ ] last_used_at updated on each authenticated request
- [ ] Audit log entry for all service account actions
- [ ] API key displayed once on creation, stored as SHA256 hash

## Technical Notes

- Service account auth is separate from user JWT auth
- Both can use Bearer token format, differentiate by token format/prefix
- Key rotation: insert new key in service_account_keys, set expires_at on old key
- Scopes checked in middleware, not at handler level

## References

- Spec: 003 Section 6 (Roles and Permissions - Service Account Security)
- Spec: 003 Section 10 (Sovereign Voice Integration - Service Account Flow)

title: Implement per-org namespace resolution in redirect handler
body:
## Description

Update the redirect handler to support org-prefixed namespaces. Single-segment paths resolve in the BrickOS org (root namespace). Two-segment paths (org-slug/code) resolve within the specified org. Also enforce reserved codes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GET /r/{code} resolves in BrickOS root namespace
- [ ] GET /r/{org-slug}/{code} resolves within the specified org
- [ ] Reserved codes return appropriate page (not 404)
- [ ] Legacy 10-char auto-codes (sha...) resolve via fast path
- [ ] Org slug validated against organizations table
- [ ] Unknown org slug returns 404
- [ ] Code unique within org, not globally (org_code unique constraint)
- [ ] Click recorded with org_id context
- [ ] Org-scoped link queries: list links WHERE owner_org_id = current_org

## Technical Notes

- Split path by '/' to determine single vs two-segment
- Index: short_links(owner_org_id, code) for org-scoped lookups
- Drop global unique constraint on code, add org+code unique constraint
- reserved_codes table checked before link lookup

## References

- Spec: 003 Section 4 (Per-Org Namespaces, Redirect Handler Logic)
- Spec: 003 Section 5 (Reserved Short URL Codes)

title: Implement platform and org-level reporting endpoints
body:
## Description

Build the reporting endpoints for three levels: platform dashboard (all orgs), org dashboard (single org), and user dashboard (personal stats). Platform admin sees cross-org aggregation. Org admin sees org-scoped metrics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] GET /api/v1/admin/stats - platform-wide stats (platform_admin only): total orgs, links, clicks, conversions, revenue by org
- [ ] GET /api/v1/admin/stats/orgs/{org_id} - single org detail stats
- [ ] GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/stats - org-level stats (org_admin+): links, clicks, conversions, top affiliates
- [ ] GET /api/v1/orgs/{org_id}/members/{user_id}/stats - member stats within org
- [ ] GET /api/v1/me/stats - personal stats across all orgs
- [ ] All stats endpoints support date range filtering (?from=&to=)
- [ ] Response includes: link count, click count, daily breakdown, top referrers
- [ ] Cross-org analytics leakage prevented: WHERE org_id enforced at all levels
- [ ] Service accounts can query stats within their scoped permissions

## Technical Notes

- Platform stats aggregate across all orgs with GROUP BY org_id
- Org stats filter by owner_org_id
- User stats filter by created_by user_id within org
- Use materialized views or denormalized counters for performance if needed

## References

- Spec: 003 Section 8 (Reporting Hierarchy - Level 0, 1, 2)

title: Implement Sovereign Voice integration API for link creation
body:
## Description

Build the service-to-service API endpoint that Sovereign Voice uses to create short links before publishing NOSTR notes. The endpoint authenticates via service account API key, creates links scoped to the BrickOS org, and returns the short URL.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] POST /api/v1/service/links - create link as service account
- [ ] Request body: target_url, org_id, code (optional), source_app, tags
- [ ] Response: { short_url, link_id, code }
- [ ] Authenticated via service account API key (Bearer token)
- [ ] Scopes required: links:create
- [ ] Rate limited per service account (rate_limit_daily)
- [ ] GET /api/v1/service/links/{code}/stats - query link stats as service account
- [ ] Scopes required: links:stats
- [ ] source_app field recorded for cross-app attribution
- [ ] Audit log entry for each service account link creation

## Technical Notes

- Sovereign Voice flow: read API key from systemd credential, POST to this endpoint, replace URL in NOSTR note, publish
- Links created by service accounts are owned by the org, not a user
- source_app enables filtering: "show me all links created by Sovereign Voice"
- Same short_links table, just with service account as creator

## References

- Spec: 003 Section 10 (Sovereign Voice Integration - Service Account Flow)

title: Implement DB consistency check queries for platform schema
body:
## Description

Build the consistency check queries that validate platform data integrity: every user has exactly one personal org, every personal org has exactly one member, no orphan links. Expose as a health check endpoint and document for nightly monitoring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Query: every user has exactly one personal org (returns 0 rows if consistent)
- [ ] Query: every personal org has exactly one member (the owner)
- [ ] Query: no orphan links (every link has a valid org)
- [ ] Query: no users without personal org
- [ ] GET /api/v1/admin/health/consistency - returns check results (platform_admin only)
- [ ] Response format: { orphan_users: 0, users_without_personal_org: 0, links_without_org: 0 }
- [ ] Checks can run as standalone SQL script for nightly cron
- [ ] Alert/warning if any check returns non-zero

## Technical Notes

- Queries use brickos schema-qualified table names
- LEFT JOIN pattern to find orphans
- GROUP BY + HAVING COUNT != 1 for cardinality checks
- Consider running as part of /health endpoint (lightweight) or separate admin endpoint (full check)

## References

- Spec: 003 Section 9 (DB Consistency - Consistency Checks)
- Spec: 004 Section 12 (Platform Health Monitoring)
